ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows two separate circles: the tangent point of the smaller circle on the left is A, and the center is O1; the tangent point of the larger circle on the right is B, and the center is O2; line AB is a common tangent slanting from upper left to lower right, and the two centers lie on opposite sides of this tangent line. Therefore AB is an internal common tangent. Since a radius is perpendicular to a tangent line, O1A and O2B are both perpendicular to AB, so O1A ∥ O2B, and their lengths are respectively 3 and 4. Because it is an internal common tangent, the perpendicular distances from the two centers to the tangent line are in opposite directions, so the component of O1O2 in the direction perpendicular to AB is 3+4=7. Given O1O2=25, the component along the tangent direction, which is the length of AB, is sqrt(25^2-7^2)=sqrt(625-49)=sqrt(576)=24. Quadrilateral O1AO2B is a trapezoid with O1A and O2B as parallel sides, the two parallel side lengths are respectively 3 and 4, and the distance between them is AB=24. Therefore the area is (1/2)(3+4)(24)=84.

method.method_draft: Decompose the area using diagonal O1O2. Let theta be the angle between AB and O1O2. Because AB is an internal tangent, the component of O1O2 perpendicular to AB equals the sum of the radii, 3+4=7. Hence sin(theta)=7/25, so cos(theta)=24/25. Since O1A and O2B are perpendicular to AB, the perpendicular distances from A and B to line O1O2 are 3cos(theta)=72/25 and 4cos(theta)=96/25, on opposite sides of O1O2. The area of quadrilateral O1AO2B is the sum of triangles O1AO2 and O1BO2, both with base O1O2=25: area = (1/2)(25)(72/25+96/25)=84.
